extraction.name: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
extraction.description: We propose TravelPlanner, a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario. It provides a rich sandbox environment, various tools for accessing nearly four million data records, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans. Comprehensive evaluations show that the current language agents are not yet capable of handling such complex planning tasks—even GPT-4 only achieves a success rate of 0.6%. Language agents struggle to stay on task, use the right tools to collect information, or keep track of multiple constraints. However, we note that the mere possibility for language agents to tackle such a complex problem is in itself non-trivial progress. TravelPlanner provides a challenging yet meaningful testbed for future language agents.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.citeAs: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su. TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.01622, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: TravelPlanner provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet that can be accessed via six tools. We also meticulously curate 1,225 diverse user queries (along with their reference plans), each imposing a different combination of constraints. The construction pipeline involves: 1)Environment and evaluation setup. 2)Diverse travel query design. 3)Reference plan annotation. 4)Quality check.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The original data for each tool is sourced from publicly available Internet data. Specifically: FlightSearch data is from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset. DistanceMatrix data is from the Google Distance Matrix API. RestaurantSearch data is from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset. AttractionSearch data is from the Google Places API. AccommodationSearch data is from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data for FlightSearch was extracted spanning from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The original data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit requirements and avoid data contamination. For FlightSearch, 'Price' was generated by multiplying 'Distance' by a random factor (0.2 to 0.5). For DistanceMatrix, 'Price' for 'self-driving' and 'taxi' was calculated by multiplying 'Distance' by factors of 1 and 0.15, respectively. For RestaurantSearch, restaurants were randomly assigned to cities and categorized under various cuisines. For AccommodationSearch, items were randomly assigned to cities and given random room rules.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Diverse queries were created starting with fundamental elements (departure city, destination, date range) randomly chosen. The duration of travel and number of hard constraints were adjusted for complexity. Natural language queries were generated using GPT-4. For evaluation, key components (transportation, restaurants, attractions, accommodations) were extracted from natural language plans and organized into a formally structured plan.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan was deemed eligible only if it met all the constraints outlined in the evaluation script. This process resulted in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors performed a detailed review of every natural language query and its corresponding annotated plan, rectifying any errors found. Each query’s budget was re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to ensure challenges.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) was used to generate natural language queries. GPT-4-Turbo was used for key components extraction from natural language plans.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research. Some data is from publicly available internet sources and does not represent the authors' viewpoints. The definition of commonsense may vary, and current evaluation criteria are based on author consensus, with encouragement for additional discussions. Evaluation scripts will be released to foster innovation. Use of evaluation feedback in the training set is encouraged, but cheating in validation and test sets is strictly prohibited to uphold fairness and reliability.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmark for complex planning and tool-use abilities of language agents.
